name: Bremelanotide (PT-141)
used_for: FDA-labeled for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD); not indicated for postmenopausal women, men, or to enhance sexual performance.

entries.text: Vyleesi: labeled dose 1.75 mg injected subcutaneously into the abdomen or thigh at least 45 minutes before anticipated sexual activity; no more than one dose in 24 hours and no more than 8 doses per month.
entries.population: Premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD

administration_guidance.text: The label states the injection is given at least 45 minutes before anticipated sexual activity.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label limits use to no more than one dose in 24 hours and no more than 8 doses per month.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label states the autoinjector is injected under the skin of the abdomen or thigh, avoiding the area within about 2 inches of the navel.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label states storage at or below 25 C (77 F), without freezing, protected from light.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: Nausea was the most common reaction in the label's trials (40% with bremelanotide versus 1.3% with placebo), typically starting within an hour of injection and lasting about two hours; vomiting occurred in 4.8%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Flushing (20.3% versus 0.3% with placebo), headache (11.3% versus 1.9%) and injection site reactions (13.2% versus 8.4%) were also common.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The label warns of transient increases in blood pressure after a dose (a peak of about 6 mmHg systolic and 3 mmHg diastolic, resolving within about 12 hours).
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The label reports focal hyperpigmentation in about 1% of patients in the trials.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: Patient reviews of Vyleesi are split: some women report increased desire, while many describe nausea, headaches and other side effects that outweighed benefits.

Forum users on a marriage-focused forum report PT-141 boosting libido in men and women, with strong erections lasting many hours and delayed onset, but also nausea and flushing, and unpredictable, dose-dependent responses.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Vyleesi (bremelanotide) injection.
research.finding: Indicated for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD; warns of transient blood pressure increases and reports nausea in about 40% of treated patients.

research.summary: RECONNECT: two randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials of bremelanotide in premenopausal women with HSDD (Kingsberg et al., Obstet Gynecol).
research.finding: Bremelanotide produced statistically significant improvements in sexual desire and reductions in related distress versus placebo; nausea, flushing and headache were most common.

research.summary: 52-week open-label extension of the RECONNECT trials (Simon et al., Obstet Gynecol).
research.finding: No new safety signals; improvements in desire and distress were sustained, with nausea (about 40%), flushing and headache the most common drug-related events.
